body.statement: Let \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)\), where \(N\geq1\), \(p\in[0,1]\), and \(0<\gamma<1\).  The two-sided equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval with total noncoverage \(\gamma\), obtained by inversion of the two binomial tails, contains \(p\) with probability at least \(1-\gamma\).

source.locator: Sections 1--2, binomial-tail inversion defining the two fiducial limits
source.verbatim_statement: It follows that in the long run of our statistical experience from whatever populations random samples of 10 are drawn, we may expect at least 95% of the points (x, p) will lie inside the lozenge shaped belt.

attestation.note: Verified against Clopper and Pearson (1934), Biometrika 26(4), pp. 405-406, public scan at http://www.barestatistics.nl/uploads/1/1/7/9/11797954/clopper__pearson_1934.pdf; equations (4)-(5) define the two binomial-tail boundaries and the quoted sentence states their at-least-95-percent coverage. The later text on p.408 also states that the confidence interval includes p with probability .95 or more.
